rounds.proof_sketch: For dim=1 with shape [16,256,256]: inner_size=256, grid.y=1, inner_idx∈[0,255]. Both 'inner_idx>=256' and 'inner_idx>=257' are always false since max(inner_idx)=255.
rounds.survival_reason: The boundary guard at line 25 protects against out-of-bounds thread indices. With inner_size=256 and the grid configuration (outer_size, ceil(inner_size/256))=(16,1), exactly 256 threads are launched per outer index, with inner_idx ranging from 0 to 255. Since inner_idx never reaches 256, both the original condition (inner_idx>=256) and the mutated condition (inner_idx>=257) are always false. The mutation only affects cases where inner_size < block_size, which would occur with dim=2 (inner_size=1), but the fixed configuration uses dim=1.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed configuration. Would require changing dim to 2 (making inner_size=1) to expose the bug where an extra thread (inner_idx=1) would execute and cause incorrect writes.
rounds.recommendations: Add mutation testing coverage for configurations where inner_size < block_size (e.g., argmax over the last dimension), as boundary guards become critical when thread counts exceed actual work items.
